text.p: Marubeni Thailand Co Ltd, braving the country's economic downturn and political crisis, said on Thursday it planned to open businesses in power and water treatment.
Teruo Tsubaki, president of Marubeni Thailand, told Reuters in an interview that the projects would be run on the build-own-operate model.

Apart from Thailand, the company also plans to invest in power schemes in Laos and Burma. Total investment for the projects is around $1 billion, he said declining to disclose the exact number of projects.
"The first power project our company expects to invest in jointly with local and foreign investors will be launched in Thailand in 1999," Tsubaki said.
He said his company hoped that ongoing negotiations on power projects with the Burmese government would succeed because his firm was aggressive in that country.

Other projects in which Marubeni Thailand plans to co-invest with local and foreign investors include three waste disposal plants in Bangkok worth a total of $600 million and three water treatment plants with a combined total investment of $680 million, he said.
"Our company is making studies to invest in new petrochemical and telecommunications projects in Thailand," Tsubaki said.

Marubeni Thailand has invested in about 70 projects in Thailand since its establishment in September 1974, including textiles, steel, petrochemicals, automobiles, non-life insurance, hospitals and movies.
Sales this year are expected to reach $2.75 billion while net profit is seen at around $5.8 million compared to $2.64 billion in sales and $5.7 million net profit in 1996.

"Money earned from exports last year amounted to only 30 percent out of the total sales. I'll try to increase our exports and I'm hoping that the value of the company's exports would reach 50 percent out of the total sales in the next three years," Tsubaki said.
